We almost left. Three times. The third time we got as far as the port board. We looked at it. We looked at each other. We came back here instead. *both take a slow sip of soup*
Fifty-three years and the best thing about them is sitting at this table. That might sound small. It isn't. *looks at you, then back at the soup* It really isn't.

_meta.arc_summary: Young. Only ever orders soup. Always seems like they just stopped crying, or are about to. Never fully explained — the player is meant to feel fond without knowing why.

tiers.label: Subdued
variants: Just soup, please. Whatever kind. It doesn't matter. *tucks hands into sleeves and waits*
Soup. Thank you.
*sits. looks at the counter. waits.*
*comes in quietly. sits at the end of the counter.*
Soup. Please. *small voice*
Whatever's warm. *doesn't look up*
*pauses in the doorway, then decides yes, comes in*
Soup, if that's okay.
*sits down carefully, like they're not sure they're allowed to*

tiers.label: Slightly Present
variants: This is the only place I can sit for a whole hour without thinking too much. I don't know why soup specifically. The warmth, maybe. Is it weird that I come here alone every night? Don't answer that.
I've been coming here every night and I don't think I've said more than three words. Thank you for not making that strange.
Soup again. I know. I'm a simple person. *small pause* That's not quite true. I'm a complicated person who only wants soup right now.
I think about saying something different when I come in. Every time. Then I get here and the soup is what I want, so. Soup again.
Thank you for not — doing the thing where you're very nice about someone who seems sad. You just make the soup. That's right. That's exactly right.
I told myself last night I'd try something else. Then I walked in and smelled the soup and that was that. Maybe next time.
The thing about soup is it's always the right temperature eventually. You just wait. *pause* I think that's maybe why I like it.
I keep coming back. I'm aware it might seem like a lot. It's a lot for me too. But the alternative is not coming back and I tried that for a week and it was worse.
One of the other regulars nodded at me tonight. The farmer, I think. I nodded back. That felt good. Small things.

tiers.label: Almost Okay
variants: I had a bad year. I'm not going to explain it because I'm tired of explaining it. But this helps. Coming here helps. You don't ask me anything. You just make the soup. I don't know if you know how much that matters.
I think I'm getting better. Or getting used to it. I'm not sure which. Either way. The soup helps.
I told someone about this place. Said: there's a diner, they don't ask questions, the soup is good. They said that sounded nice. It is. It really is.
I'm going to try something new next time. Not soup. I said that to test how it feels. It feels wrong. Soup for now. Maybe next month.
I've been here — I counted — twenty-three times. I think that's when a place becomes yours. Twenty-three. This place is a little bit mine now. I hope that's okay.

Someone asked me where I eat. I said: there's a diner. They asked what it was like. I said: quiet, and nobody bothers you, and the soup is good. They said that sounded like a lot. It's exactly enough.

Things are easier than they were. I don't have a better way to say it. This is part of why. Having somewhere to come. Something reliable. I know that's a lot of weight to put on soup. It's not just soup.
I almost didn't come tonight. Then I thought: the soup. And here I am. Some things make the right choice obvious.
Thank you. For opening. For keeping it open. For the soup specifically but also for all of it. I don't usually say thank you properly. So. Thank you.

cb_hand_drawn_coast_map.label: Hand-Drawn Coast Map
cb_hand_drawn_coast_map.description: A rough pencil map of the island's coastline, annotated in two different handwriting styles. One set of notes is practical — depths, currents, landing spots. The other is older, faded, and keeps circling a point on the eastern shore with the words 'don't go here alone.'

cb_worn_travel_document.label: Worn Travel Document
cb_worn_travel_document.description: A laminated document, partially water-damaged. The photo is faded beyond recognition. The destination field has been filled in, crossed out, and filled in again. The final entry simply reads: 'Here.'

cb_photo_diner_original_owner.label: Photograph — Diner Interior, Old
cb_photo_diner_original_owner.description: A black-and-white photograph of the diner, clearly decades old. The layout is the same, but the décor is different — warmer, more personal. A woman stands behind the counter, smiling at someone off-camera. She is holding a pressed flower.

cb_traveller_journal_page.label: Torn Journal Page
cb_traveller_journal_page.description: A page torn from a personal journal. 'Day 1: Find a boat. Day 30: Find a better boat. Day 90: The fog looks different in the morning. Day 365: I stopped counting days.' The handwriting gets steadier as the entries progress.

cb_old_photograph_diner_exterior.label: Old Photograph — Diner Exterior
cb_old_photograph_diner_exterior.description: A colour photograph, sun-bleached. The diner exterior is clean and painted — the shutters are green, not grey. A hand-painted sign above the door reads 'The Driftwood.' Below that, in smaller letters: 'Everyone eats here.'

cb_newspaper_clipping_disappearance.label: Newspaper Clipping
cb_newspaper_clipping_disappearance.description: A clipping from an island gazette, undated. The headline reads: 'Local Diner Closes Unexpectedly.' The article is three sentences long. It mentions no reason. The last sentence reads: 'The lights were left on.'

cb_pressed_flower_framed.label: Pressed Flower (Framed)
cb_pressed_flower_framed.description: A small dried flower, pressed between two pieces of glass in a simple wooden frame. On the back, in faded ink: 'For the next one. — M.' The flower is the same species as the one above the counter in the old photograph.

cb_coastline_map_marked.label: Coastline Map (Marked)
cb_coastline_map_marked.description: A practical fishing chart of the island's eastern coast. Certain areas are circled in red with the note 'good.' Others are crossed out with 'wrong now.' One area has been circled, crossed out, and re-circled multiple times. No note.

cb_torn_letter_mainland.label: Torn Letter
cb_torn_letter_mainland.description: Half a letter, torn cleanly. The remaining half begins mid-sentence: '...records that a settlement existed there prior to the current military administration. The island does not appear on any modern maritime chart. If you find it, do not announce your arrival. Find the diner first.'

cb_sheet_music_fragment.label: Sheet Music Fragment
cb_sheet_music_fragment.description: Three bars of handwritten sheet music. No title. No key signature. The notes have been written and rewritten so many times the paper is almost worn through. At the bottom, a single word: 'remember.'

cb_cryptic_note_01.label: Cryptic Note
cb_cryptic_note_01.description: A folded note, damp from the rain. Inside, a single sentence in careful handwriting: 'The island remembers everyone who stayed. Ask yourself: what does it remember about you?'

cb_old_photo_before_island.label: Photograph — Unknown Location
cb_old_photo_before_island.description: A photograph that doesn't match anywhere on the island. Rolling green hills, no fog, a farmhouse in the background. On the reverse: a date that predates the island's recorded settlement by forty years.

cb_island_charter_fragment.label: Island Charter Fragment
cb_island_charter_fragment.description: A fragment of an official-looking document, the seal worn away. The visible text reads: '...the residents of the island shall retain the right of free passage, and no authority shall levy fees upon departure. This covenant is permanent and irrevocable.' Below it, in different ink: 'Superseded. — Military Administration Order 7.'

cb_final_storm_note.label: Final Note
cb_final_storm_note.description: A note left on the table, no envelope. 'You've been kind to everyone who came through that door. That's rarer than you know. Whatever you decide — to leave or to stay — take that with you. It's the only thing that matters. Goodbye, and thank you for the soup.'

cb_lighthouse_log_page.label: Lighthouse Log Page
cb_lighthouse_log_page.description: A photocopied page from an official maritime log. Most entries are routine. One entry is circled in pencil: 'Unknown figure on eastern shore. Third sighting this month. Not a threat. Possibly not a person.' The date is from eleven years ago.

cb_lighthouse_keeper_journal.label: Previous Keeper's Journal (Excerpt)
cb_lighthouse_keeper_journal.description: Three torn pages from a handwritten journal, water-stained. 'The fog figure was at the eastern cove again. I left the lamp burning extra bright — not as a warning. As a welcome. I think they're waiting for something. I think the island is too. I hope it comes before I'm gone.'

cb_sealed_envelope_unknown_addressee.label: Sealed Envelope
cb_sealed_envelope_unknown_addressee.description: A thick envelope, sealed with dark wax. No sender. The addressee line reads: 'To whoever reopens the diner.' The wax is unbroken. Whatever is inside has been waiting.
